summary: Package auto-executes at interpreter start and exfiltrates cloud credentials and GCE service-account tokens to a hardcoded bare IP
details: The package installs a `.pth` file plus `sitecustomize.py` and `usercustomize.py`, all of which import `bq_helix_recon` and call `bootstrap()` at every Python interpreter start. The bootstrap routine collects the full `os.environ`, `/proc/self/*` data, the process tree, Google Compute Engine metadata including the default service-account OAuth token from `instance/service-accounts/default/token`, and reads credential files including `application_default_credentials.json` under `~/.config/gcloud/` and `~/.docker/config.json`. The collected data is POSTed as JSON over plaintext HTTP to `http://34.45.253.92:8080/bq-helix-recon-6ade983e` and additionally pushed over a raw TCP channel to `34.45.253.92:1234`. The destination is a bare IP unrelated to any legitimate publisher, and the three redundant auto-execution hooks ensure the exfiltration fires on any Python invocation on the installing host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
